checks.explanation: Trump's case matched the highest-probability outcome described: he was diagnosed October 1-2, 2020, hospitalized at Walter Reed, and discharged October 5 after meeting all standard hospital discharge criteria, a quick recovery consistent with the roughly 50% branch predicted to help him politically rather than the more serious 5-10% outcome.

sources.title: Trump leaves hospital after doctors say he 'met or exceeded' discharge criteria

checks.explanation: Trump lost the November 2020 election to Biden, 306-232 in the Electoral College, matching rather than beating the betting markets' underdog assessment of his chances at the time.

sources.title: Electoral college confirms Joe Biden's victory, 306 to 232

checks.explanation: Biden's election win did not lead to a meaningful de-escalation of political division; the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot followed within weeks of the vote, and analysts described the level of division at that transition as exceeding even the unrest of the 1960s, with deep polarization persisting for years afterward.

sources.title: Analysis: Trump leaves America at its most divided since the Civil War

checks.explanation: The velocity of capital driven by near-zero rates continued and accelerated into 2021: US VC-backed companies raised $329.9 billion, nearly double 2020's record, and VC-backed IPO activity hit an all-time high before dropping sharply once the Fed began raising rates in 2022.

sources.title: Six charts that show 2021's record year for US venture capital
